A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-DA research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning results on commonsense and mathematical reasoning benchmarks in Tables 1–4, together with convergence, rank, component-ablation and Fisher-sample analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a layer-type initialization ablation on GSM8K in Appendix I, Table 8.

M1.justification: The Fisher-based bias and variance components, initialization objective, K-FAC approximation, LOBPCG solver and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Selective layer initialization is introduced as an ablation, without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both retain Commonsense170K and MetaMathQA training, the eight commonsense benchmarks, GSM8K, MATH and the MNIST trajectory experiment. The new layer ablation uses existing GSM8K coverage with different initialization configurations.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain LoRA, PiSSA, MiLoRA and LoRA-One, the ChatGPT reference row, and the LoRA-FA frozen-A comparator. The new layer experiment uses existing LoRA and LoRA-DA controls plus within-method ablations.

E3.justification: The new GSM8K ablation applies LoRA-DA initialization only to attention layers or only to FFN layers, while other layers use standard random initialization. Existing benchmark protocols and hyperparameters, shown in v2 Table 9 and v3 Table 10, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds Appendix I and Table 8 to test how initialization benefits differ between attention and FFN layers. The existing component ablation, rank sweep, training-dynamics analysis, MNIST trajectory experiment and Fisher-sample sensitivity study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. The new ablation also reports point estimates only; the Fisher-sample sensitivity study already appears in v2.

E6.justification: v3 Table 8 newly reports GSM8K scores of 53.8 for attention-only initialization and 54.3 for FFN-only initialization, alongside the existing random-initialization and full LoRA-DA scores of 53.1 and 55.0. Existing benchmark, timing, component-ablation, Fisher-sensitivity and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds an explicit trace-based derivation of the projection-norm identity in v3 Equation 45, supplying an intermediate proof step previously implicit between v2 Equations 43–44. The assumptions, theorem statements and final bounds are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same theoretical and algorithmic contributions and claims about accuracy, convergence, rank robustness and initialization overhead. The stated average improvements of 0.3 percentage points for NLU and 1.0 for NLG remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The added attention-versus-FFN statement summarizes the new ablation's observed ranking without introducing a mechanism explanation or substantive limitation. Existing interpretations of training dynamics, rank effects, Fisher stability and applicability to other PEFT methods are unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising code release upon publication to stating availability and supplying a repository address. However, v3 Appendix L retains the future-release wording, and actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs. Existing hardware and implementation settings are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. Changes to LQ-LoRA's publication information, Compacter's author formatting and bibliographic entry, and WinoGrande's metadata refer to existing works rather than adding or removing research.

P1.justification: v3 expands the projection explanation, adds a short layer-ablation subsection and pointer, corrects theorem references, and updates appendix references. It also adds conflict-of-interest and funding statements and replaces the preprint notice with proceedings information. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the layer-ablation Table 8 and moves the existing Table 7 to the same appendix page. Subsequent tables are renumbered and material reflows across pages. Existing figures and table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The new layer ablation provides useful evidence about where initialization helps beyond v2's component ablation, while the explicit projection calculation and corrected references make the reasoning easier to verify. These are limited gains with the core method and benchmark results unchanged. The new code pointer improves access information, although contradictory future-release wording remains in Appendix L.
